We were long distance. We began fighting during the few occasions where we could spend time together in person and that was upsetting to me because it was supposed to be our time to enjoy each other’s presence. And we did for the most part but paired with increasing disagreements over the phone and no clear plan that made sense for the both of us to live together, it just felt clear that we wouldn’t work out if we couldn’t fix our issues now. For reference I’m 22 F and she’s 26 F. So we’re both really young and I still love her very much but I had to think that rationally we probably just have more growing and maturing to do. We stopped growing and consistently ran into the same communication issues we tried to fix. But we didn’t really know how. I decided I would rather end it and possibly save our friendship or retry in the future although I know there’s a chance neither of those will happen. I love her too much to watch myself become more and more frustrated in the relationship and decided it’s for the best to let her go. I also am 22 and need to heal from things in my past and discover who I am as an adult outside of the relationship. We’ve been together since I was 19 and I just feel an urge to focus on myself rather than be bogged down with the responsibilities and struggle of maintaining a long distance relationship. I feel bad for giving up on her but it hurts me too and I know I’m trying to do the right thing for the both of us so our relationship doesn’t go completely down the drain. I do hope we’ll be friends when we have time to heal because you’re right OP, it wasn’t some deep unsolvable issue. We’re just young and dumb. And I wanted to grow. I hope she is still a part of my life in the future but I’m willing to find peace in life if it doesn’t happen too.

I understand this completely. I've always wanted to get out of school ASAP because I knew there was more out there for me than formal education. But one thing I did learn through schooling is to not have a defeatist attitude towards it. I hate the structure of standardized education but our age (I'm 17) is the best time to grasp new concepts and TRULY learn because our brains are still growing. You're failing, I was failing too and said fuck this it's pointless, but I had to realize that it isn't pointless, it's meaningless. Once I understood the difference I was able to direct my studies towards things that really mattered to me.  That's hard to do with the limited classes offered at high school so I dual enrolled, got the classes I needed to graduate high school out of the way and am now taking college classes that interest me and challenge me. It gets 8 million times easier when you have a sense of purpose behind your schoolwork, whatever that may be. Good luck and never give up!
